Meet the Governors
Meet the Governors
Welcome to our Governors’ section
Please find below details of how our Governing body is structured, including the names, categories, responsibilities and terms of appointment for each Governor.
In accordance with the Government’s requirements for all governing bodies, the core strategic functions for Westfield School Governing Board are:
1. Ensuring clarity of vision, ethos and strategic direction
2. Holding executive leaders to account for the educational performance of the school and its pupils, and the performance management of staff; and
3. Overseeing the financial performance of the organisation and making sure its money is well spent In addition, the governors undertake to:
4. Ensure the safety of all members of the school community in accordance with the ‘Keeping Children Safe in Education’ Act (2015) Governance Arrangements
The governing board of Westfield School is made up of 12 Governors, all serving a four year term of office.
This breaks down to:
• 2 staff governors (including the Headteacher)
• 2 elected parent governors
• 1 Local Authority governor
• 7 co-opted governors
The full governing board meets at least twice a term and the minutes are available from the School upon request. The Pay Committee meets annually to consider the recommendations from the annual performance management reviews.
Other additional committees / panels relating to pupil and staff discipline, parental complaints etc are convened when required.

Music
Focussed Beats – A music project provided by CreateED, funded by the Rothschild Foundation.
Focussed Beats is a dynamic and inclusive music programme designed for children with autism spectrum condition (ASC). The programme supports social and communication development, enhances wellbeing, and nurtures musicality.
Outcomes for participating children include:
Increased confidence as music makers
Greater motivation to engage and learn
Enhanced social skills and interactions
Improved communication abilities
Active participation in focused interaction and attention-based activities
Development of language, performance, and musical skills
Positive impact on health and wellbeing
Improved emotional regulation and reduced behavioural challenges
Weekly group sessions are led by an experienced music leader and include musical games and activities that build interaction, knowledge, confidence, and performance skills.

Frequently asked questions
I am looking for a school for my child. Can I come for a tour? Yes, we offer information sessions and a tour every half term for prospective parents. The session is at 4 o’clock in the afternoon and you can meet the headteacher and have a look around the school. We do not offer tours during the school day due to safeguarding our students.
If you would like to book onto the next open evening, please email the school office:
office@westfield.bucks.sch.uk
Can the headteacher/ assistant head call me to discuss my child and their needs / look at my paperwork?
If you would like to know more about us and if we would be the right setting for your child, please feel free to explore our website and view the Prospective Parents presentation. You are also invited to come to our next Prospective Parents open evening. Please email the school office to book a place.
We are only permitted to view a child’s paperwork once we are officially consulted through the Local Authority.
How do I apply for a place for my child at your school? Please see the flowchart attached. At time of publication, this information was accurate to the best of our knowledge from the local authority.
admissions-to-westfield.pdf
We do not live in Buckinghamshire – how do we apply for a place at Westfield?
Please see the flowchart for admissions. If you are outside of Buckinghamshire, your Local Authority will consult with Buckinghamshire County Council directly.
Does my child have to have an EHCP to apply to Westfield?
Yes, all of the children at Westfield have an EHCP already in place.
Do you have spaces now? If not, do you have a waitlist? No, we are full and over capacity. We are a Local Authority Maintained school, all of our spaces are allocated by Buckinghamshire County Council through the consultation process and placement panel.
How big are the classes?
What is the staff ratio to children?
Class sizes at present are between 8 and 12 children. There is a ratio between 1.5 children to 1 adult, and 3 children to 1 adult, depending on the class and provision needed for that group.
How are therapies delivered at Westfield (ie. Speech and Language Therapy or Occupational Therapy)?
At Westfield, we run an integrated therapies approach:
This means that in every lesson children will take part in a therapeutic learning activity related to their Speech and Language skills, Occupational therapy needs, etc.
Please use the link below to learn more about therapies and interventions at Westfield.
Provision | Westfield School
Do you run breakfast/after school?
No, we do not provide wraparound care.
I am a Westfield parent. How best to contact the school? Please see the table below for the best way to contact school:
By email or phone to office
office@westfield.bucks.sch.uk
Do you automatically take siblings?
No, we do not. Every child must go through the consultation process.
How does my child get transport?
If you would like your child to have transport to school, this is done through the Transport Team in the SEN department of Buckinghamshire County Council. Please discuss this with your EHCCO.
What is the criteria for children to move from Apple, to Pear, to Cherry?
Our children are grouped by need, and not by year group. We group the children by what provision we need to have in place in that classroom, and then differentiate the curriculum and learning.
Moreover, the numbers are not progressive. Think of the numbers as a street address! Pear 1, 2, 3, does not mean that Pear 3 is harder work or higher in the curriculum than Pear 2 and 1. When you enter Pear base, Pear 1 is the first classroom you see, then Pear 2, then Pear 3, etc.
How do I buy a jumper?
You are able to buy new school jumpers through Arbor.
I am a Westfield parent, how do I apply for a place for my child for Secondary School?
There is an information session for our parents when their child is in Year 5. Please come along and ask all your questions about Secondary transfer.

Please see the email below from Buckinghamshire Council All Age Disabilities Team:
We are hosting our Access All Areas events again this month (see attachment).
It is an event aimed at showcasing what information, support, housing and activities are available to help people of all ages who are autistic or have a learning disability, to stay healthy, fulfilled (physically, mentally and emotionally) and remain as independent as possible.
The events will be hosted across two venues, The Gateway (Aylesbury) on Monday 16th October and the Highcrest Academy (Wycombe) on Thursday 26th October. The events will be in a market stall format with over 40 organisations signed up to participate, the details of which can be found on our website: Access All Areas | Buckinghamshire Council. The stalls are set over a number of rooms to help the event not feel overwhelmingly busy.
